data.title: RBI steps up gold loan scrutiny as bullion rout signals borrower stress
data.description:
By Siddhi Nayak
 
India’s banking regulator is stepping up scrutiny of the nation’s $247 billion gold-loan sector as a sharp drop in bullion prices erodes the collateral that lenders demand from borrowers, according to people familiar with the matter. 
The Reserve Bank of India’s supervisory officers have reviewed early indicators of stress, asset quality and loan amounts against pledged gold, the people said, asking not to be identified as they are not authorised to speak to the media. 
 
Banks and shadow lenders can lend as much as 85 per cent of the metal’s value, and the RBI has been checking protectively if this is being breached, though no evidence has been found yet, the people said. The RBI did not immediately respond to an emailed query.
 
 
The regulator’s stricter watch coincides with signs of distress among borrowers that shadow lenders spotted in the quarter ended September. An amended rule that barred deferred interest repayment has also contributed to delinquencies. The pressure has mounted as gold collapsed 30 per cent since its January peak, with the rout accelerating in recent weeks on expectations of a more hawkish US Federal Reserve. 
 
A record rally in the precious metal had fanned the borrowing boom. The gold lending industry expanded almost fivefold in five years to ₹23 trillion ($247 billion), with about 60 per cent of the market still informal, according to a report by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. on Friday. The segment accounts for about 2.5 per cent of India’s bank credit as of September, limiting any systemic risk. 
 
The stress in gold credit portfolios is expected to persist over the next few quarters, the people said.
 
A drop in gold prices can leave loans insufficiently backed, forcing borrowers to pledge additional collateral or repay part of their debt. A prolonged decline increases the risk of delinquencies, potentially leaving lenders including IIFL Finance Ltd. and Bajaj Finance Ltd. exposed to losses.
 
IIFL Finance’s nonperforming assets in the gold portfolio edged higher to 0.9 per cent of total loans as of end-September, from 0.6 per cent in the prior quarter, according to its quarterly result disclosures. At Bajaj Finance, India’s biggest shadow lender, the share of gold loans facing repayment stress rose to 2.02 per cent from 1.87 per cent, filings showed.
 
Piramal Finance CEO Jairam Sridharan said in an analyst call last month that gold loans are emerging as an important area of emerging risk.

data.title: Bisleri disputes FSSAI test findings over West Bengal sample, seeks probe
data.description:
Packaged drinking water maker Bisleri on Saturday said independent tests by two accredited laboratories found its West Bengal water sample compliant with quality standards and urged food regulator FSSAI to examine the reasons for differences in lab findings. 

ALSO READ: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri again after Bengal sample fails

Bisleri International Pvt Ltd's statement follows the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)'s latest order sanctioning prosecution against the company after a regulatory sample collected from West Bengal failed in lab testing.

Sources on Friday said a sample collected from its manufacturing facility at Telipara in Jalpaiguri district was found to contain coliform bacteria.

 

Both the primary and referral laboratories reported the presence of coliform bacteria in the sample, following which the regulator prohibited the sale of the specific batch (PB201) on August 12, 2026, they said.

Responding to the FSSAI's latest order, Bisleri on Saturday said in a statement that it had already recalled the said batch of its packaged drinking water at the direction of FSSAI, which was prohibited on 12 August 2026.

The Chauhan family-led firm said independent testing of samples from the same batch yielded different results.

"Bisleri separately commissioned independent testing of samples from the same batch at an FSSAI-recognised laboratory, which found that the sample met the applicable standard for coliform bacteria and all other applicable food safety standards," the company said.

Moreover, samples tested at another independent, FSSAI-recognised laboratory also reported that the sample met the applicable standard for coliform bacteria.

"The difference between the regulatory and independent findings warrants a thorough review," Bisleri said, calling upon FSSAI to examine the sampling process, testing methodology, laboratory findings and any factors that may have contributed to the variation in results.

The company said it expected the matter to be "assessed against the same standards" applied across the industry and would continue to cooperate fully with FSSAI to establish the facts.

Earlier, the food regulator had sanctioned prosecution against the company after a sample collected from one of its manufacturing facilities in Goa was found non-compliant with prescribed food safety standards.

In the Goa case, FSSAI had said the sample was non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared it unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

Following a Bisleri appeal, the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory, which also classified it as unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), according to the regulator.

Meanwhile, FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani recently said the regulator was collecting packaged drinking water samples from across the country, with laboratory testing expected to be completed within one to two months.

He emphasised that enforcement actions were aimed at ensuring compliance with food safety standards and did not create panic among consumers.

The central food regulator has also communicated with state food commissioners and regional directors to step up surveillance, inspection and sampling of packaged drinking water and mineral water, and take action against companies in cases of non-compliance.

FSSAI has been intensifying enforcement measures against food business operators and e-commerce companies this year as part of its efforts to strengthen food safety oversight across the country.

data.title: India, UK researchers to develop nanorobots for targeted drug delivery
data.description:
Researchers at the UK's Imperial College London and the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Bengaluru have joined forces to develop nanorobots that can be steered through the body or other complex environments using magnets.

The collaboration, announced by Imperial this week, combines synthetic biology with nanorobotics to create microscopic systems that can move, carry materials and potentially deliver them to precise locations.

The technology could eventually support new approaches to targeted medicine, biosensing and environmental monitoring.

"Synthetic cells offer an exciting way to recreate some of the remarkable functions of living cells," said Dr Claudia Contini, from the Department of Life Sciences at Imperial College London.

 

"Adding magnetic nanomotors could give these systems a new ability to move and respond to their surroundings. By working closely with our partners at IISc Bengaluru we hope to create controllable, life-like technologies with future applications in medicine and environmental sensing," she said.

"Professor Ghosh and his team are internationally recognised for developing magnetic nanorobots that can operate in complex biological environments. His group has demonstrated nanorobotic systems moving through human blood and inside living cells," the engineering biologist noted.

Professor Ambarish Ghosh, a leading expert in magnetic nanorobotics at IISc Bengaluru, said his team has learnt how to steer magnetic nanorobots through blood, tissue and even inside living cells, but they are fundamentally inorganic in nature.

"Dr Contini's synthetic cells can carry and release cargo in ways an inorganic robot cannot. Together they give us a platform that can be guided to a target and made to act there. We are delighted to be working with Dr Contini and her group, and grateful to Imperial for supporting this partnership," he said.

Under the collaboration, the team aims to build hybrid systems that combine the flexibility of artificial cells with the movement of tiny magnetic motors. These motors would act like miniature engines inside cell-like compartments, helping the structures travel through difficult environments and carry out specific tasks when directed.

Synthetic cells are carefully engineered structures that reproduce some of the useful features of living cells. But most synthetic cells cannot move by themselves or travel towards a chosen target. The new project will explore whether that can be changed by placing magnetic nanomotors inside polymer-based vesicles microscopic compartments that resemble biological cells.

One problem with current therapeutics is that when drug molecules enter the bloodstream they can diffuse and travel all around the body, which can cause unwanted side effects. By using external magnetic fields to guide the synthetic cells, researchers could then control exactly where they go and what they do. This could result in lower doses being needed and reducing the impact of potential side effects.

Dr Contini's research group develops life-like systems from the bottom up, designing artificial cells that mimic selected properties and functions of living cells. Her work brings together synthetic biology, bioengineering and active matter, with a focus on biomedical and biotechnological applications.

This latest India-UK project is supported by Imperial's India Connect Fund, with researchers at both institutions sharing expertise, training and facilities. The project aims to create a long-term research platform connecting synthetic biology and nanorobotics, supporting future projects, student training and knowledge exchange between the UK and India.

data.title: Bisleri seeks FSSAI review over conflicting test results for Bengal batch
data.description:
Bisleri International has sought a review by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over conflicting laboratory findings concerning a batch of its packaged drinking water manufactured at its facility in Telipara, Jalpaiguri district, West Bengal.
 
The development comes after the regulator prohibited the sale of the specific batch, identified as PB201, on August 12, 2026, following the detection of coliform bacteria in samples tested by its primary and referral laboratories. The FSSAI has also sanctioned prosecution against the company in the matter, according to reports.
 
“Bisleri International Private Limited had already recalled Batch PB201 of its packaged drinking water at the direction of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which prohibited the sale of the batch on 12 August,” the company said in a statement.
 
 
Bisleri said that while the primary and referral laboratories reported the presence of coliform bacteria in the regulatory sample, independent tests commissioned by the company yielded different results.
 
The company said it had separately commissioned testing of samples from the same batch at an FSSAI-recognised laboratory, which found that the sample met the applicable standards for coliform bacteria and other food safety parameters.
 
Samples tested at another independent, FSSAI-recognised laboratory also met the prescribed standards, it added.
 
“The difference between the regulatory and independent findings warrants a thorough review. Bisleri calls upon FSSAI to examine the sampling process, testing methodology, laboratory findings and any factors that may have contributed to the variation in results,” the statement said.
 
“We expect this matter to be assessed against the same standards applied across the industry,” the company added, reiterating that it would continue to cooperate with FSSAI to establish the facts.
 
Bisleri said it maintained stringent quality controls involving more than 90 tests across its 10-step manufacturing process and asserted that its products remained safe for consumption.
 
This is the second recent instance of regulatory action by FSSAI against Bisleri over the quality of its packaged drinking water.
 
On Sunday, the food regulator said it had sanctioned prosecution against the company following the detection of bromate levels above permissible limits in a sample collected from its Goa manufacturing facility. Subsequent testing by a referral laboratory also flagged the presence of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), according to the regulator.
 
The Goa case relates to a batch manufactured in September 2025 at the company's facility, one of its 143 manufacturing plants.
 
Bisleri had said FSSAI collected six samples from the facility on September 30, 2025. Initial testing found that five samples met the applicable standards, while the sixth recorded bromate levels of 12 micrograms per litre against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.
 
Following an appeal by the company on November 22, 2025, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory for retesting.
 
The referral laboratory found bromate levels within the prescribed limit but separately flagged the presence of PAHs, the company said.
 
On November 23, FSSAI clarified that bromate levels in the retested sample were below the permissible limit. Bisleri subsequently welcomed the clarification, while pointing out that one of six samples tested in a subsequent round had reported PAHs at 0.144 micrograms per litre. Another sample from the same batch cleared all parameters.
 
The company said it had sought a retest of the PAH findings and that subsequent samples tested by FSSAI across its manufacturing facilities had not reported adverse PAH findings.
 
The two cases involve separate batches and manufacturing facilities, with the latest dispute concerning coliform bacteria in the West Bengal batch and the earlier one involving bromate and PAH findings in the Goa batch.

data.title: Maritime security vital for global trade, economy, says President Murmu
data.description:
President Droupadi Murmu on Saturday said the maritime domain had become increasingly important in today's interconnected world, with a large part of global trade moving through the seas, and stressed that India was steadily strengthening its indigenous defence capabilities.

Addressing the passing-out parade of the Indian Naval Academy (INA) at Ezhimala here, she said the security of maritime routes was closely linked to the economic well-being of nations and the everyday lives of their people.

"The maritime domain has become increasingly important in today's interconnected world. A large part of global trade moves through the seas. The security of maritime routes is therefore closely linked to the economic well-being of nations and the everyday lives of their people," she said.

 

President said that any disruption in the movement of ships can affect the supply of essential goods, increase costs, and ultimately place an additional burden on ordinary citizens.

"You should remember that your service at sea is connected to the lives of the people of India. It contributes directly to their security, prosperity, and well-being," she said.

The President said India was also steadily strengthening its indigenous defence capabilities, with a growing number of ships and submarines being designed and built in Indian shipyards.

"This reflects our commitment to self-reliance and our confidence in the capabilities of our engineers, scientists, skilled workers, and industry. As an officer of the Indian Navy, you will be part of this journey towards a stronger and more self-reliant India," she said.

Noting that the world was changing at an unprecedented pace, Murmu said new technologies were transforming the nature of warfare and maritime security.

"We cannot predict all the challenges that the future will bring, but I am confident that your training, adaptability, and commitment will prepare you to face them. You should always continue to learn and should keep upgrading your knowledge and skills," she said.

The President said the ultimate purpose of all national efforts was to build a strong, prosperous and developed India.

The vision of Viksit Bharat was not limited to economic growth or improvement in development indicators. It was about creating a nation where every citizen felt secure, had access to opportunities and could lead a life of dignity and self-respect, she said.

It was also about ensuring that the benefits of development reached every section of society and every corner of the country, she said Referring to her participation in the International Fleet Review in Visakhapatnam in February this year, Murmu said it was an impressive demonstration of the Indian Navy's growing strength and capabilities.

India was making rapid progress in strengthening its armed forces and enhancing its maritime capabilities, she said.

Murmu expressed happiness over the presence of several young women among the graduating trainees and said their participation was a matter of pride for the entire nation.

"My dear daughters, your presence here is a matter of pride for the entire nation. You have demonstrated that determination, courage, and competence know no boundary. Your achievements will inspire many more young women to dream big and take up challenges and responsibilities in the service of the nation," she said.

Congratulating the graduating cadets, the President said they had successfully completed training that tested their physical endurance, mental strength and determination.

Their smart turnout, excellent military bearing and precision in performing the drill reflected the highest standards of training, discipline and dedication, she said.

Murmu also acknowledged the contribution of the parents and families of the graduating officers, saying that behind every young officer stood a family that had made sacrifices, offered encouragement and provided strength through difficult times.

She extended special congratulations to the trainees from friendly foreign countries and said it was heartening to see them marching shoulder to shoulder with their Indian counterparts.

"The friendships developed at the academy would go beyond the years spent there, and the trainees would carry forward the spirit of mutual trust, cooperation and friendship that bound their countries together, she said.

The President said the integrity, professional competence, courage and compassion of the officers would define the character of the Indian Navy.

"You should always remember that leadership is not merely about giving commands. It is about undertaking responsibility, setting an example, and standing by those who serve with you," she said.

A total of 427 officer trainees passed out as commissioned officers at the Indian Naval Academy.

Murmu first reviewed the platoons before receiving the salute from the marching contingent.

She also presented awards to the best-performing cadets at the academy, Keralam Governor Om Prakash Mathur, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Southern Naval Command, Vice Admiral Sameer Saxena, and Commandant of the Indian Naval Academy, Vice Admiral Alok Ananda, were also present.

data.title: Binance gets preliminary approval to establish Asia hub in Bhutan
data.description:
Binance said ??on Friday it received in-principle approval ​from Bhutan's Gelephu Central Bank to establish regulated digital-asset operations in the Himalayan kingdom, ??as part of its plans to expand into five Asian markets next year. 
"The in-principle approval is a first step, not a full license ‌, and Binance must satisfy the ​conditions specified by GCB... ​before the relevant regulated activities may commence," the world's largest cryptocurrency ​exchange said in a statement. 
Binance's expansion push follows a security breach US authorities have linked to North Korea that resulted in $6.3 billion being stolen from its platform last month and stopped all ​users from making withdrawals for the next two days. The company ‌said earlier this week it has finished work to ​recover its withdrawal systems. 
 
This month, SB Seker, head of Binance's Asia-Pacific unit, told Reuters: "We have ongoing conversations with at least five or six markets... three ‌of which are in ​quite mature stages." 
Seker did ‌not specify the new markets that Binance was looking at. Binance ‌has ??operating licences in 15 markets, and Seker said South ​and Southeast Asia were key priorities. 
The partnership in Bhutan will include an operational presence, with local hiring ​and investment in digital assets, the Binance statement on Friday said. 
"Establishing an Asia hub in Gelephu Mindfulness ‌City is a strategic decision that reflects Binance's commitment to operating within ‌clear, progressive regulatory frameworks", Seker said in the statement. 
Binance has said it could cover the losses linked to the October cyberattack without raising fresh funds.

data.title: India 3rd largest foreign user of SIAC with 178 parties: Singapore minister
data.description:
India ranks as the Singapore International Arbitration Centre's (SIAC) third-largest foreign user jurisdiction, with 178 Indian parties involved in its arbitrations last year, Singapore's Minister for Law and Second Minister for Home Affairs Edwin Tong said on Friday.
 
Speaking at the Indian Council of Arbitration's (ICA) symposium on 'India-Singapore: From Shared Legal Foundations to the Future' in Singapore, Tong highlighted India's growing participation in international arbitration and called for greater innovation by institutions, practitioners and courts to address the complexities of cross-border commercial disputes.
 
He said investors need the assurance that disputes arising from their investments would be resolved fairly, transparently and predictably. India has long been among SIAC's most important foreign user jurisdictions, with Indian counsel and arbitrators also participating in cases that do not involve any Indian parties, he added.
 
 
Tong also highlighted the challenges posed by complex, multi-contract transactions, where interconnected disputes can end up being heard in separate forums, potentially leading to inconsistent outcomes.
 
He called for ways to resolve disputes involving interconnected parties more effectively while preserving the fundamental principle of party consent in arbitration.
 
"Arbitration is built on party consent. So how do we preserve that principle whilst ensuring that interconnected parties and their disputes can be resolved effectively?" he said.
 
"India and Singapore should aspire not merely to succeed in international arbitration, but to make international arbitration better," Tong added.

CJI calls for stronger cooperation

In a video message to the symposium, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice Surya Kant called for greater cooperation between India and Singapore in arbitration, mediation and institutional development.
 
He said the two countries could exchange experiences in institutional design, professional standards, training and technology, while encouraging the early use of mediation to resolve commercial disputes.
 
"Predictability in dispute resolution is not an afterthought to commerce, it is part of the confidence that enables it," the CJI said.
 
Highlighting the economic ties between the two countries, Justice Surya Kant said bilateral trade had increased from about $6.7 billion in 2004-05 to $34.3 billion in 2024-25.
 
Singapore also remains a major source of foreign investment into India, with cumulative foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows of about $174.88 billion between April 2000 and March 2025, accounting for around 24 per cent of India's total inflows, he said.
 
The CJI said India's growing engagement with mediation, including the establishment of the Mediation Council of India, offered further opportunities for cooperation between the two countries. He also highlighted the potential of multi-tiered dispute resolution clauses, which provide for mechanisms such as mediation before arbitration.
 
"Sometimes the best outcome is not a victory for one side, but an agreement that enables both sides to move forward," he said.
 
Referring to the 2024 Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in Law and Dispute Resolution between India and Singapore, the first meeting of the India-Singapore Joint Consultative Committee in 2025, and the ICA's India-Singapore ADR Conclave held in New Delhi on September 10, 2026, Justice Surya Kant said bilateral cooperation should be based on reciprocity.
 
"Neither needs to replicate the other's institutional model. The opportunity is to learn from each other. The corridor must be a two-way channel for expertise, professional opportunities and institutional knowledge, measured by the confidence it creates on both sides," he said.

Legal cooperation linked to trade ties

ICA President and Senior Advocate Dr N G Khaitan said a shared legal future between the two countries depended on strong economic and trade ties.
 
He highlighted Singapore's predictable regulatory environment, commercial dispute resolution mechanisms and enforcement of law, noting that the country accounted for about 24 per cent of equity FDI into India.
 
"It is a win-win situation for all of us," Khaitan said.
 
ICA Director General Arun Chawla said the symposium marked 200 years since Singapore's Second Charter of Justice was granted on November 27, 1826.
 
He identified four pillars of the India-Singapore partnership: economy and enterprise; emerging technology; energy and environment; and exchanges and engagement, with trust connecting them.
 
"Commerce needs confidence, investment needs certainty, and both need assurance of justice," Chawla

data.title: Pawan Kalyan backs delimitation reform, says it will strengthen democracy
data.description:
Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan expressed support for the proposed delimitation reform, saying it would strengthen democratic representation by giving every state and region an adequate voice in Parliament.

The deputy CM said a stronger democracy is built when every citizen is heard, and every state moves forward with confidence.

"The proposed delimitation reform will strengthen democratic representation by ensuring that every state and region has an adequate voice in Parliament," said Kalyan in a post on X late on Friday.

He said the proposed reform, ahead of the special Parliament session scheduled for November 30, envisaged a 50 percent increase in Lok Sabha seats across all states while maintaining their existing proportional representation until 2051.

 

The proposed framework would create more opportunities for representation while protecting the proportional share of southern states, which have made progress in population stabilisation, he said.

According to the Deputy CM, the proposal reflected the spirit of cooperative federalism by recognising the contributions and progress of different states while ensuring that their parliamentary representation was protected.

He also welcomed the proposed 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies, saying it would boost their participation in decision-making.

Crediting Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju for driving inclusive institutional reforms, Kalyan urged all political parties, elected representatives and other stakeholders to set aside political differences and support the initiative in the larger interest of democracy.

He called for a more representative and inclusive Parliament in which every state had a respected voice and all sections of society had opportunities to participate.

data.title: Tata Sons files caveats after Bombay HC refuses relief to Tata trusts' plea
data.description:
Tata Sons has filed caveats in the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court on Saturday, ensuring it will be heard if two Tata trusts file an appeal, according to sources.

The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and RD Tata Trust could not get any relief from the Bombay High Court on Friday, which said it would not pass any order deferring or granting an injunction on the November 30 board meeting of Tata Sons.

The trusts had sought for the meeting to be deferred and/or for an order restraining Chandrasekaran from exercising his casting vote.

"Caveats filed by Tata Sons Pvt Ltd in Bombay High Court and Supreme Court in relation to order dated 27 Nov 2026," as per a person in the know.

 

The two Tata trusts can move the courts in appeal, and the caveats will help Tata Sons present their side in the matter.

A bench of Justice Abhay Ahuja of the Bombay HC on Friday did not grant any immediate relief to the two Tata trusts and said that the meeting can go on as scheduled, but the same would be subject to the final orders of the court.

The Tata trusts had sought to defer or stay the meeting, or an order that the chairman would not be allowed to exercise his casting vote.

The bench ordered Tata Sons and the other respondents in the case, which include the board members, to submit their reply affidavits to two suits filed on Thursday (November 26) and posted the matter for further hearing on January 18, 2027.

The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the RD Tata Trust (RDTT) had filed the suits in the High Court against Tata Sons and six of its directors, challenging the reappointment of Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term.

The SDTT has sought Rs 50 crore, while the RDTT has demanded Rs 15 crore in damages, with 18 per cent annual interest, from Tata Sons.

As per the suits, the September 17 Tata Sons board resolution reappointing Chandrasekaran was invalid because it did not receive the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association (AoA).

The immediate relief sought was to prevent the chairman of Tata Sons from exercising his casting vote during the November 30 board sitting in the event of a split in opinion among nominee directors of Tata Trusts.

On Friday, the trusts' counsels also sought for the meeting to be deferred, which was opposed by Tata Sons.

Noel Tata, the chairman of Tata Trusts, is battling against Tata Sons, the holding company of the country's largest conglomerate in which the trusts have a 66 per cent ownership, over issues including the reappointment of Chandrasekaran and also trying to avoid a listing of the company.

The RBI has mandated the listing of Tata Sons after classifying it as an NBFC-Upper Layer, and Noel has been pressing for a restructuring of the business to avoid the IPO.

data.title: Indian markets rebound in November after months of underperformance: HSBC
data.description:
Indian financial markets have staged a broad-based recovery in November, reversing months of underperformance against emerging-market peers as falling crude oil prices, a correction in global artificial intelligence-related investments and renewed foreign fund inflows improved investor sentiment, HSBC Global Investment Research said.

Equities, the rupee and government bonds have all rallied, signalling a shift in market sentiment from risk-off to risk-on.

However, sustaining the gains into 2027 will require stronger domestic growth expectations and an improvement in banking-system liquidity, which could remain constrained as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) tightens monetary policy amid elevated inflation, the global brokerage said.

"India has moved from risk-off to risk-on. After underperforming the EM Index for most of 2026, Indian markets rebounded in November, outperforming across equities, FX and rates. The recovery was supported by falling oil prices, global investors de-risking from AI names and stronger foreign inflows," it said.

 

India had underperformed emerging markets across equities, foreign exchange and interest rates for much of 2026 before staging a sharp turnaround in November.

The Sensex has gained around 13 per cent month-to-date, while the rupee strengthened to its highest level in eight months, trading below 92.50 against the US dollar.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year government security fell by around 20 basis points, indicating a rally in bond prices despite tightening liquidity conditions.

The recovery has been supported by lower international crude oil prices and global investors reducing exposure to artificial intelligence-related stocks, both of which have helped improve sentiment towards Indian assets and encouraged foreign capital flows.

HSBC said the simultaneous improvement across equities, currency and government bonds, along with a positive correlation between equity and debt returns, points to a broad-based improvement in risk appetite.

The return of foreign investors has been a key factor behind November's market rebound, particularly in equities, although debt markets have also seen improved inflows.

Domestic investors have supported Indian markets over the past few years, helping cushion the impact of foreign portfolio outflows.

"While domestic investors are needed to make sure the markets don't fall, sharp increases in returns are typically led by foreign investor participation," the brokerage said.

HSBC's analysis using the Diebold-Yilmaz framework, which measures the transmission of shocks between different asset classes, found that currencies are the largest net transmitter of market shocks in India.

The latest recovery followed a similar pattern, with the rupee beginning to strengthen around the middle of October, ahead of the broader improvement in other asset classes.

The brokerage's multi-asset analysis suggests that the November rebound was not driven by one isolated market development but reflected improving sentiment across financial markets, with currency movements playing an important signalling role.

HSBC, however, cautioned that external factors alone may not be sufficient to sustain India's market performance in the coming year.

Its proprietary multi-asset model identifies two global and two domestic variables that explain a substantial part of returns across Indian asset classes. The model currently indicates that Indian equities remain undervalued relative to their model-implied returns.

The rupee and government bonds, in contrast, appear broadly fairly valued.

This suggests that equities have greater scope to catch up if the current favourable conditions persist. However, once the valuation gap closes, further gains will depend on an improvement in the variables driving the model's expected returns.

HSBC identifies banking-sector liquidity and expectations of potential economic growth as the two key domestic factors that need to improve.

Liquidity could remain under pressure as the RBI tightens monetary policy in response to elevated inflation, potentially limiting the availability of funds in the banking system.

Consequently, stronger growth expectations will become increasingly important in sustaining investor returns.

The brokerage sees a possible improvement in India's export competitiveness and foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows as potential catalysts.

India's goods exports rose 25 per cent year-on-year in the previous quarter, supported by a more competitive currency, trade agreements and exporters expanding into new markets.

HSBC said the increase in exports, alongside early signs of stronger FDI inflows, could help improve expectations of India's longer-term growth potential.

If these trends strengthen, they could provide the domestic economic support needed to sustain higher returns across Indian asset classes in 2027.

However, risks remain, including the possibility of renewed escalation in geopolitical tensions pushing oil prices higher and a revival of volatility in global technology stocks. HSBC remains positive on the AI theme for 2027 despite the recent correction.

Against this backdrop, HSBC's equity strategists remain overweight on Indian equities, citing resilient corporate earnings and more reasonable valuations following the period of underperformance.

The brokerage believes the improvement in valuations, combined with the prospect of sustained earnings growth, provides support for the market despite uncertainties surrounding global conditions and domestic liquidity.

Its rates strategists, meanwhile, have introduced a pay-five-year Non-DeliverableOvernight Index Swap (NDOIS) trade, reflecting expectations of tighter monetary policy amid the RBI's focus on inflation.

In foreign exchange, HSBC's strategists have lowered their USD-INR forecasts for the end of 2026 and 2027, signalling a more favourable outlook for the Indian currency.

The brokerage also prefers the rupee among Asian currencies in the deficit-currency category, reflecting its relative attractiveness in regional foreign-exchange carry trades.
